newsitem.title: ITALY: CIS 1996 cereals and pulses output up 2 pct - FAO.
newsitem.headline: CIS 1996 cereals and pulses output up 2 pct - FAO.

text.p: The United Nation's Food and Agriculture Organisation said in a report released on Thursday it expected aggregate 1996 output of cereals and pulses in the Commonwealth of Independent States to be two percent above 1995 production.

The report, dated November 4 and based on data collected during a mission to the CIS in September, said it estimated output would be 133 million tons cleaned weight, compared with 130 million last year.
It forecast substantially better harvests in Russia and Kazakhstan but sharp falls of between 18-50 percent in Moldova, Turkmenistan and the Ukraine.

FAO estimated that CIS wheat production could rise in 1996 by 70 million tons, thanks both to higher yields and expanded area. The aggregate output of coarse grains is expected to decline five percent to 58 million tons, the report said.
Overall food supplies in the CIS remained adequate to meet demand during 1995-96.

It said that following the poor harvest in 1995, aggregate imports of cereals in 1995-96 are estimated to have risen nearly 12 million tons including intra-CIS trade, a rise of 1.2 million tons on the preceding year.
FAO estimated that cereal utilisation would contract in 1996-97 to an estimated 157 million tons compared with 172 million in the preceding year and 238 million in 1991-92.
CIS cereal import requirements for 1996-97 are tentatively estimated at 9.2 million tons including intra-CIS trade, some 2.7 tons less than imports in 1995-96, FAO added.

It projected Russian wheat imports of three million tonnes, of which 500,000 tonnes would be imported from outside the CIS. Coarse grain imports would be 800,000 tonnes including 200,000 tonnes from outside the former Soviet Union.
